info.title: ZeroSettle IAP API
info.description: The ZeroSettle IAP API powers the iOS, Android, and Flutter SDKs. It enables product catalog fetching, web checkout, entitlement management, subscription lifecycle operations, and StoreKit transaction syncing. All endpoints are authenticated via the `X-ZeroSettle-Key` header.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Fetch the product catalog for your app

tags.name: Checkout
tags.description: Create checkout sessions and payment intents for web purchases

tags.name: Entitlements
tags.description: Query user entitlements (active purchases and subscriptions)

tags.name: Cancel Flow
tags.description: Configurable cancel flow with retention offers

tags.name: Identity
tags.description: Move a guest's purchases to their account (reconcile two ids)

get.description: Fetches the product catalog for your app, including web, StoreKit and Google Play prices, trial details, checkout configuration and any active Switch & Save or upgrade offer for the user. Pass `user_id` to get per-user trial eligibility and offers.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The user's external ID. When provided, the response includes per-user `is_trial_eligible` on each product.

parameters.name: storefront
parameters.description: Two-letter storefront country code (for example `US`). Send it so the displayed price, routing and trial match what checkout will charge for region-specific pricing and experiments.

parameters.name: demo
parameters.description:
**Debug-only.** Surfaces a dashboard-configured campaign as if the requesting user were eligible for it, regardless of their real subscription state. Lets developers preview their tip UI without crafting a specific test account.

- `migration` returns the configured `MigrationCampaign` (Switch & Save) on `config.migration` (and `config.offer` mirror with `flow_type=migration`).
- `upgrade` returns the configured `UpgradeOfferConfig` (Upgrade & Save) on `config.offer` with `flow_type=upgrade`. Uses the first `upgrade_paths` entry as the preview source/target. `savings_percent` is `0` for demo previews — accurate proration requires a real billing cycle.
- Honored **only** on test-mode publishable keys (`zs_pk_test_*`). Live keys silently ignore the flag. Impressions are NOT counted on demo requests. Any other value (including the legacy `true`) drops the bypass and the normal user-state resolver runs.

migration.description: Active Switch & Save campaign for this user, or null when the user is anonymous or not eligible.

offer.description: Unified offer for this user (Switch & Save or upgrade), or null when the user is anonymous or not eligible. New SDKs prefer this over `migration`.

post.description: Creates a Stripe PaymentIntent (or SetupIntent for free trials) for web checkout. Returns the `client_secret` and a `checkout_url` for the hosted checkout page. SDK 1.3.0 and later send `X-ZS-SDK-Version` and get `410 use_checkout_configs` here: the SDK uses a different endpoint for those versions and handles it itself, so you only call this endpoint directly from a custom integration.

external_user_id.description: The user's external ID. Either this or `user_id` is required.

user_id.description: Alias for `external_user_id`. Either this or `external_user_id` is required.

platform.description: The platform the purchase is being made from.

stripe_customer_id.description: Existing Stripe customer ID to attach the payment to.

customer_name.description: Optional customer display name to attach to the Stripe customer for this checkout. Also accepts the camelCase alias `customerName`.

customer_email.description: Optional customer email to attach to the Stripe customer for this checkout. Also accepts the camelCase alias `customerEmail`.

checkout_mode.description: `native` (default) returns a `checkout_url` for the embedded checkout page shown in the SDK web view. `browser` returns a URL for the same checkout opened in a browser.

storekit_subscription_end.description: ISO 8601 datetime of the current StoreKit subscription's expiry. Used for Switch & Save migrations to align the trial period.

storekit_original_transaction_id.description: The StoreKit original transaction ID for the subscription being migrated.

external_purchase_token.description: Apple externalPurchaseToken received from StoreKit at the disclosure-sheet confirmation step. When provided, ZeroSettle uses this token for automatic external-purchase reporting in eligible jurisdictions (EU/EEA under the DMA alternative terms, EEA music streaming, and Japan MSCA on iOS 26.4+). Optional — omit for non-Apple platforms or regions where reporting is not required.

ios_version.description: iOS version of the checkout client (e.g., '26.4.1'). Used for JP MSCA regime gating, which requires iOS 26+. Optional.

storefront.description: Two-letter storefront country code. Used for region-specific pricing and experiments.

rc_app_user_id.description: RevenueCat app user ID, if using the RevenueCat integration.

play_purchase_token.description: Google Play purchase token for the subscription being migrated (Android Switch & Save).

400.description: Invalid request. Includes `code` values `customer_conflict` and `invalid_customer` (bad `stripe_customer_id`) and `stripe_account_restricted` (connected Stripe account setup is incomplete).

403.description: `code` is `tenant_disabled` (merchant account disabled) or `not_whitelisted` (live key on an account not yet approved for live transactions). A routing experiment can also return 403 `Web checkout is not available for this user`.

409.description: `already_entitled`: the user already has an active entitlement for this one-time product. Or `in_flight`: a checkout for this user and product is being prepared; retry after `retry_after` seconds.

410.description: `use_checkout_configs`: the request carried `X-ZS-SDK-Version` 1.3.0 or later. SDKs of that version use a different endpoint and handle this themselves.

500.description: `checkout_domain_not_configured`: the server has no checkout domain configured.

503.description: `migration_unavailable` (Switch & Save is unavailable right now) or server busy with `retry_after`.

post.description: Creates Stripe PaymentIntents for multiple products in a single request. Reduces N sequential requests to 1, with shared Stripe customer/account resolution. Products that fail validation return an error entry instead of failing the entire batch. Maximum 25 products per request.

products.description: Array of products to create payment intents for. Maximum 25 items.

storekit_subscription_end.description: ISO 8601 datetime of the current StoreKit subscription's expiry. Used for Switch & Save migrations.

storekit_original_transaction_id.description: The StoreKit original transaction ID for the subscription being migrated.

platform.description: The platform the purchase is being made from.

stripe_customer_id.description: Existing Stripe customer ID to attach payments to.

customer_name.description: Optional customer display name to attach to the Stripe customer for this batch. Also accepts the camelCase alias `customerName`.

customer_email.description: Optional customer email to attach to the Stripe customer for this batch. Also accepts the camelCase alias `customerEmail`.

rc_app_user_id.description: RevenueCat app user ID, if using the RevenueCat integration.

200.description: Batch results with per-product success or error

results.description: Array of results, one per requested product. Each entry is either a successful PaymentIntent response or an error object.

client_secret.description: Stripe PaymentIntent client secret. Present on success.

transaction_id.description: ZeroSettle transaction ID. Present on success.

amount.description: Charge amount in cents. Present on success.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. Present on success.

product_name.description: Display name of the product. Present on success.

original_amount.description: Full price before discounts/trials. Present on success.

checkout_url.description: Fallback URL for browser-based checkout. Present on success.

publishable_key.description: Stripe publishable key for confirming the payment. Present on success.

stripe_account.description: Connected Stripe account ID for BYOS. Null for managed mode.

merchant_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for Apple Pay.

is_subscription.description: Whether this product is a subscription. Present on success.

subscription_interval.description: Subscription billing interval (e.g., `month`, `week`). Present for subscriptions.

trial_type.description: Type of trial applied. Omitted when no trial.

trial_end.description: Unix timestamp when trial ends. Only present with active trial.

pending_amount.description: Amount billed when trial ends. Only present with active trial.

error.description: Error code or message. Present when this product failed, for example `in_flight` or `already_entitled`.

callback_url.description: URL the checkout page returns to after payment. Present on success.

charge_amount.description: Cents the intent charges or holds now. Present for trial checkouts.

intent_type.description: Which Stripe confirm method to call. Present on success.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with an `in_flight` error entry.

400.description: Invalid request, or Stripe account setup incomplete (`code` `stripe_account_restricted`).

post.description: Creates a Stripe Checkout Session for browser-based checkout. Returns a URL to redirect the user to Stripe's hosted checkout page.

external_user_id.description: The user's external ID. Either this or `user_id` is required.

user_id.description: Alias for `external_user_id`. Either this or `external_user_id` is required.

platform.description: The platform the purchase is being made from.

stripe_customer_id.description: Existing Stripe customer ID to attach the payment to.

rc_app_user_id.description: RevenueCat app user ID, if using RevenueCat integration.

storefront.description: Two-letter storefront country code. Used for region-specific pricing and experiments.

play_purchase_token.description: Google Play purchase token for the subscription being migrated (Android Switch & Save).

storekit_subscription_end.description: ISO 8601 expiry of the StoreKit subscription being migrated.

storekit_original_transaction_id.description: Original transaction ID of the StoreKit subscription being migrated.

400.description: Invalid request (missing `product_id` or user id, or `stripe_customer_id` not starting with `cus_`).

403.description: `code` is `tenant_disabled` (merchant account disabled) or `not_whitelisted` (live key on an account not yet approved for live transactions). A routing experiment can also return 403 `Web checkout is not available for this user`.

409.description: `already_entitled`: the user already has an active entitlement for this one-time product. Or `in_flight`: a checkout for this user and product is being prepared; retry after `retry_after` seconds.

500.description: `checkout_domain_not_configured`: the server has no checkout domain configured.

get.description: Retrieves the status of a transaction by the `transaction_id` returned from checkout. Poll this after a checkout to confirm the payment settled.

parameters.name: transaction_id
parameters.description: The transaction ID (UUID returned from checkout).

patch.description: Reports a StoreKit subscription state change for a migration transaction. As of 2026-04-27, this is a *trigger to verify* endpoint: when the SDK reports `storekit_status=2` (anything other than active), the backend queries Apple's App Store Server API itself and persists what Apple reports onto the transaction's `storekit_apple_status` and `storekit_subscription_end` fields. Billing-relevant data is never sourced from the client.

storekit_status.description: `1` = active (finished successfully, no further action). `2` = anything-not-active (cancelled, expired, billing retry, grace period, revoked). When `2` is reported, the backend triggers a server-side Apple App Store Server API query to resolve the canonical state.

storekit_original_transaction_id.description: Apple `originalTransactionId` for the subscription. Used by the backend to query Apple's API for the canonical subscription state when `storekit_status=2`. Optional — the backend will fall back to the value stored at transaction creation time when omitted.

storekit_subscription_end.description: Deprecated as of 2026-04-27. Accepted for backwards compatibility but **ignored** — the backend now resolves the actual subscription expiry from Apple's App Store Server API. Existing SDKs may continue sending this field; new SDKs should omit it.

400.description: `storekit_status` is not 1 or 2, or the body is not valid JSON.

get.description: Returns up to `limit` transactions for a user, most recent first. There is no cursor. Abandoned checkout sessions (a checkout replaced by a newer one for the same product) are not returned, and a disputed transaction is reported as `refunded`. Look a user up by `user_id`, or by `email` for legacy email-only checkouts.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The user's external ID. Send either `user_id` or `email`.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Customer email. Matches only transactions recorded with that email (legacy email-only checkouts). Prefer `user_id`; email-only lookups are deprecated.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of transactions to return. Default: 50, Max: 100.

400.description: Neither `user_id` nor `email` was sent.

get.description: Returns the entitlements a user currently has access to: active subscriptions and one-time purchases. Entitlements that have expired or are paused are not returned. Use this to decide what the user can access.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The user's external ID. Required unless `email` is provided.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: The user's email address. Deprecated: use `user_id`. An email lookup matches only legacy email-only checkouts (identities with no external user id), so a user your app identified with a user id is never found by email.

pending_actions.description: Follow-up actions for the app to show, for example cancelling an old store subscription after Switch & Save. Empty when there are none.

post.description: Transfers an existing StoreKit entitlement to the calling user. Used when an Apple ID's StoreKit subscription is owned by a different ZeroSettle account and needs to be moved to the current account (account migration, support flows, sandbox testing). The backend verifies the supplied JWS, revokes the entitlement from the previous owner, and grants it to `user_id` in a single atomic transaction. The bundle id in the JWS is checked and logged on claim but does not refuse the request, unlike Sync StoreKit Transaction.

jws_representation.description: The StoreKit 2 transaction's JWS representation string for the entitlement being claimed.

user_id.description: The external user ID that should receive the entitlement.

claimed.description: True if the entitlement was transferred to the current user. False when the entitlement already belonged to the current user (no-op).

product_id.description: Reference ID of the claimed product. Present when `claimed` is true.

original_transaction_id.description: StoreKit `originalTransactionId` of the claimed entitlement. Present when `claimed` is true.

message.description: `Already owned by this account` when nothing moved. Present when `claimed` is false.

entitlement_states_transferred.description: Number of entitlement rows moved to the user. Present when `claimed` is true.

transactions_reassigned.description: Number of transactions reassigned to the user. Present when `claimed` is true.

400.description: Bad request. The error is one of: `Invalid JSON body`; `jws_representation is required`; `user_id is required`; `Cannot claim entitlement to a synthetic identity` (a `user_id` starting with `apple_otid:`); `Consumable products cannot be claimed`; `Missing productId in JWS payload`; `No originalTransactionId in JWS`.

401.description: Invalid API key, or JWS verification failed: `JWS signature verification failed`.

404.description: `No entitlement found for this transaction`: nothing is recorded for the JWS `originalTransactionId`, so there is nothing to claim.

post.description:
Forwards a StoreKit 2 JWS (JSON Web Signature) transaction to ZeroSettle for verification and recording. The backend verifies the JWS against Apple's root certificate chain, creates a `Transaction` and `Entitlement`, and returns success. The SDK should call `transaction.finish()` only after receiving a success response.

SDK 1.3+ additionally forwards `will_auto_renew` (pulled from `Product.SubscriptionInfo.RenewalInfo.willAutoRenew`) on every sync. The backend diffs this against the stored entitlement state and emits `CANCELLED` / `REACTIVATED` events when the flag flips, so auto-renew state stays accurate even in deployments without App Store Server Notifications (ASSN) v2 configured.

jws_representation.description: The StoreKit 2 transaction's JWS representation string.

will_auto_renew.description: Optional (SDK 1.3+). The current `willAutoRenew` value from StoreKit's `Product.SubscriptionInfo.RenewalInfo` for the subscription this JWS belongs to. When provided, the backend compares it against the stored entitlement and emits `CANCELLED` (true→false) or `REACTIVATED` (false→true) events. Omit the field for non-subscription syncs or older SDKs; behaviour is unchanged when missing.

renewal_state.description: Optional (SDK 1.3+, reserved). Mirror of StoreKit's `Product.SubscriptionInfo.RenewalState` for future use. Accepted but not currently acted on. Typical values: `subscribed`, `expired`, `in_billing_retry_period`, `in_grace_period`, `revoked`.

transactions.description: Bulk reconcile mode: send this instead of `jws_representation`. Each entry has `signed_transaction` and optionally `signed_renewal_info`. See the notes on this page.

customer_name.description: Optional. Used to fill the customer name when none is recorded. Also accepts `customerName`.

customer_email.description: Optional. Used to fill the customer email when none is recorded. Also accepts `customerEmail`.

schema.description: Send either `jws_representation` (a single transaction) or `transactions` (bulk reconcile). `user_id` is always required.

200.description: Transaction synced successfully, or a conflict was reported. If `owned` is `false` with `conflict: true`, another user already owns this Apple subscription: nothing was granted, and `claim_available` tells the app it can offer Claim Entitlement.

owned.description: `true` when the entitlement now belongs to `user_id`. `false` when another user owns it (see `conflict`).

original_transaction_id.description: Apple `originalTransactionId` of the subscription or purchase.

resolved_via.description: How an ownership change was resolved on the server: `none` for an ordinary sync, or a value such as `apple_verified_ownership_change` or `orphan_auto_resolve`. Informational.

is_test_purchase.description: `true` when Apple processed the transaction as a sandbox purchase (TestFlight, App Review or Xcode) but the request used a live key. The purchase is saved in Live as a test purchase and is left out of revenue.

conflict.description: `true` when another user owns this Apple subscription. Present only on a conflict.

claim_available.description: Present on a conflict: the app can offer Claim Entitlement.

existing_owner_hint.description: Present on a conflict: a short non-reversible hash that identifies the other owner without revealing it.

warning.description: Present when the Apple environment does not match the key.

400.description: Bad request. `error` is `Invalid JSON body`, `jws_representation is required`, `user_id is required` or `Missing productId in JWS payload`. With `code` `bundle_id_mismatch`: the JWS `bundleId` does not belong to this app (see below).

401.description: Invalid API key, or JWS verification failed: `JWS signature verification failed`.

409.description: The StoreKit transaction id already belongs to a different project, so it cannot be recorded here. Nothing is saved.

message.example: This StoreKit transaction id already belongs to a different project.

get.description: Returns the current status of a StoreKit subscription by its original transaction ID. Useful for checking renewal state and expiry. The response includes normalized `is_active` and `auto_renew_enabled` booleans (SDK 1.2+); prefer these over the raw `status`/`auto_renew_status` fields for canonical access decisions.

parameters.name: original_transaction_id
parameters.description: The StoreKit original transaction ID for the subscription.

400.description: `original_transaction_id` query parameter is missing.

502.description: The lookup against Apple failed or returned nothing (`Failed to query Apple subscription status`).

get.description: Canonical offer + subscription-state resolver (SDK 1.2+). Returns the user's current subscription variant plus exactly one offer decision (`no_action`, `migrate_storekit_to_web`, `migrate_play_to_web`, `upgrade_storekit_to_web`, or `upgrade_web_to_web`). Replaces the overlapping `/iap/products/` offer config, `/iap/upgrade-offer/`, and ad-hoc status parsing with a single typed contract. Legacy endpoints remain supported for older SDKs.

post.description: Records that a Switch & Save migration was completed. It counts a conversion on the campaign. It does not record impressions.

variant_id.description: The experiment variant ID, if the migration campaign is part of an A/B test.

source.description: The storefront the user migrated away from. Defaults to `store_kit`.

conversions.description: Total number of conversions for this campaign.

400.description: `source` is not `store_kit` or `play_store`.

404.description: `No migration campaign found` for this environment and variant.

post.description: Cancels a user's web checkout (Stripe) subscription. By default access continues until the end of the current billing period. Set `immediate: true` to cancel now. A Switch & Save migration trial is always cancelled immediately. App Store and Google Play subscriptions cannot be cancelled here: they return 400 `No Stripe subscription linked`.

product_id.description: Specific product to cancel. If omitted, cancels the user's active subscription.

immediate.description: If `true`, cancels immediately and revokes access. If `false`, cancels at end of billing period.

400.description: `user_id is required`, `Invalid JSON body`, or `No Stripe subscription linked` (the subscription was not bought through web checkout).

post.description: Pauses a user's web checkout (Stripe) subscription. With `pause_duration_days` it resumes automatically after that many days; without it the pause is indefinite until Resume Subscription is called.

product_id.description: Specific product to pause. If omitted, pauses the user's active subscription.

pause_duration_days.description: Number of days to pause. If omitted or 0, the subscription is paused until you resume it.

400.description: `user_id is required`, `Invalid JSON body`, or `No Stripe subscription linked`.

post.description: Resumes a previously paused web checkout subscription.

product_id.description: Specific product to resume. If omitted, resumes the user's paused subscription.

400.description: `user_id is required`, `Invalid JSON body`, or `No Stripe subscription linked`.

post.description: Creates a Stripe Customer Portal session URL. The portal lets users manage their subscriptions, update payment methods, and view billing history.

return_url.description: URL to redirect the user to after they leave the portal.

portal_url.description: URL to redirect the user to the Stripe Customer Portal.

404.description: `No billing record found for this user`. Only web checkout subscribers have a billing portal.

get.description: Returns the cancel flow configured in your dashboard: survey questions, a retention offer, pause options and, on current SDKs, deflection and downgrade blocks. When the flow is disabled or not configured the response is `{"enabled": false}`. The shape depends on the SDK: see the notes on this page.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The user's external ID. Used to personalize offers.

parameters.name: storefront
parameters.description: Two-letter storefront country code, used for geo-targeted experiments.

post.description: Submits the user's responses from the cancel flow, including survey answers and the final outcome (cancelled, retained, dismissed, or paused). Used for cancel flow analytics.

outcome.description: The final outcome of the cancel flow.

offer_shown.description: Whether a retention offer was shown to the user.

offer_accepted.description: Whether the user accepted the retention offer.

pause_shown.description: Whether a pause option was shown.

pause_accepted.description: Whether the user chose to pause.

pause_duration_days.description: Number of days the user chose to pause, if applicable.

last_step_seen.description: Index of the last cancel flow step the user saw. Defaults to 0.

variant_id.description: Experiment variant ID, if the cancel flow is part of an A/B test.

question_id.description: ID of the question, from Get Cancel Flow.

selected_option_id.description: ID of the chosen option, from Get Cancel Flow.

free_text.description: Free-text answer, if the question allows one.

400.description: `Invalid JSON body`, `user_id is required`, or `outcome must be cancelled, retained, dismissed, or paused`.

post.description: Accepts the retention offer from the cancel flow and applies it to the user's Stripe subscription: a percentage discount for a number of months, or a free period. Calling it again for a subscription that already carries the offer returns the offer that is applied.

product_id.description: The product the offer applies to.

message.description: Human-readable summary, for example `20% off for 3 months`.

discount_percent.description: Percent discount applied. Null for a free-period offer.

duration_months.description: Months the discount lasts. Null for a free-period offer or a forever discount.

400.description: `user_id is required`, `product_id is required`, `Save offer is not enabled`, `No Stripe subscription linked`, or `Invalid offer configuration`.

404.description: `Cancel flow not configured`, or `No active subscription found`.

get.description: Checks whether a user can be offered a subscription upgrade and returns the offer. `available` is `false` with a `reason` when there is no offer.

parameters.name: product_id
parameters.description: Specific product to check upgrade eligibility for.

400.description: `user_id query parameter is required`.

post.description: Starts the upgrade. For a web subscription (`web_to_web`) the existing Stripe subscription is changed to the target plan in place, with proration, and the response carries the new entitlement. There is no client secret. For an App Store subscriber (`storekit_to_web`) the response tells the app which product to check out: call Create Checkout Session or Create Payment Intent for `target_product_id`, then show the cancel instructions.

current_product_id.description: The reference ID of the user's current subscription product.

target_product_id.description: The reference ID of the product to upgrade to.

400.description: `user_id`, `current_product_id` or `target_product_id` is missing, or the upgrade could not be performed (the message is in `error`, for example `Target product not found`).

post.description: Records that the user declined or dismissed an upgrade offer, for analytics. Accepting an offer is recorded by Execute Upgrade Offer, not here.

variant_id.description: Experiment variant ID, if the upgrade offer is part of an A/B test.

outcome.description: What the user did with the offer.

current_product_id.description: Reference ID of the user's current product.

target_product_id.description: Reference ID of the offered product.

400.description: `Invalid JSON body`, `user_id is required`, `outcome must be 'declined' or 'dismissed'`, or `current_product_id and target_product_id are required`.

post.description: Tracks a funnel event from the SDK. `event_type` must be one of `paywall_viewed`, `checkout_started` or `checkout_abandoned`. `event_type`, `user_id` and `product_id` are all required.

event_type.description: The funnel event type. Any other value returns 400.

user_id.description: The user's external ID. Up to the current SDK release, events sent before `identify` use the literal `anonymous`. From the next SDK release, SDKs send a per-device UUID (the SDK's `analyticsUserId`) instead, the same one `identify(.anonymous)` adopts later. A guest-to-account reconcile moves these events to the account.

product_id.description: The product the event relates to. Required.

environment.description: Optional. The StoreKit environment the device is running in (`Production`, `Sandbox` or `Xcode`), sent by the iOS SDK from the next SDK release. A non-production environment sent with a live key marks the event as a test event. Omitted when unknown, and an omitted value is never treated as a test event.

screen_name.description: The screen or view where the event occurred.

metadata.description: Additional key-value metadata for the event.

400.description: `Invalid JSON body`; `event_type, user_id, and product_id are required`; or `Invalid event_type. Must be one of: ...`.

post.description:
Moves purchases made by an anonymous (email-only) customer to the current user ID, matched by email. Useful when a user reinstalls the app or signs in on a new device. The ZeroSettle SDKs do not call this endpoint: it is for your own restore flow.

Each matching guest identity is moved through the same reconcile core as Reconcile Identities. If the guest and the target hold a live entitlement to the same non-consumable product (a subscription, including a trial or one cancelled but still running out its period, or a one-time unlock; consumables never conflict), that guest is refused and **nothing is restored from it**. The response is still `200`. `restored` counts only what moved (so it is `0` when every match was refused), and `message` tells the person to contact support.

A move that happens sends an `identity.reconciled` webhook, not `subscription.purchased`. The guest's Stripe links and profile are not moved by this endpoint.

Rate limited per IP (10 an hour), per email and app (5 an hour) and per app (6,000 a minute). Over a limit the response is `429` with a `Retry-After` header. If the rate-limit store is unavailable, the per-IP and per-email limits refuse the call with `429` and `Retry-After: 5`. A restore button should treat a `429` as a failed restore and offer a retry after the delay.

email.description: The user's email address to match against previous purchases.

user_id.description: The user's current external ID to restore purchases to.

restored.description: Number of entitlements restored. `0` when nothing matched or every match was refused.

target_identity_id.description: The ZeroSettle identity id of the user restored to. An integer, including when a conflict refused the restore. Absent only when no guest purchases matched the email.

message.description: A short human-readable result. On a refused conflict: `Some purchases could not be restored automatically. Contact support.`

value.message: Some purchases could not be restored automatically. Contact support.
No anonymous purchases found for this email

400.description: `Invalid JSON body`, or `email and user_id are required`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. `5` when the rate-limit store is unavailable.

error.example: Too many restore attempts. Try again later.

get.description: Server-to-server. Lists the users who are currently eligible for your Switch & Save offer, so your backend can target them (for example with email or push). Authenticate with your **secret** key, never the publishable key. The environment (sandbox or live) comes from the key. This is an enumeration: it does not count impressions. Eligibility follows the same rules as the offer the SDK shows. When no campaign is enabled the list is empty.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor: the `next_cursor` from the previous page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Default 100, maximum 500. Values below 1 are raised to 1.

external_user_id.description: The user ID your app passed to `identify`.

product_id.description: The product the user subscribes to.

eligible_since.description: When the user became eligible: the start plus the campaign minimum subscription days.

is_currently_eligible.description: Always `true`: only eligible users are listed.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. Null on the last page. A page can hold fewer users than `limit` only on the last page.

is_enabled.description: Whether the Switch & Save campaign is enabled.

401.description: The `X-ZeroSettle-Key` header is missing, or the key is not a valid secret key (`Invalid secret key`). A publishable key is rejected.

post.description:
Moves one id's purchases, credits, analytics and experiment rows onto another id, from your server. Call it when a guest signs up and you know the guest id and the account id are the same person.

Authenticated with your **secret key** (`zs_sk_*`), sent in `X-ZeroSettle-Key` or as `Authorization: Bearer`. Never call it from an app. A publishable key is refused with `401 secret_key_required`.

The merge is one way, and an id that has been merged away cannot be merged again. If both customers hold a live entitlement to the same non-consumable product (a subscription, including a trial or one cancelled but still running out its period, or a one-time unlock; consumables never conflict), the call is refused and nothing moves. Stripe and the stores are never changed. If `from` has no customer record at all (no purchase, checkout or Stripe customer), only its analytics and experiment rows move: the call succeeds with zero counts, sends no event and sets up no forwarding. A guest with a customer record but no purchases takes a normal merge, with zero counts, forwarding and an `identity.reconciled` event. Purchased credits move and add to the account's balance; plan allowances do not move.

**Idempotency.** Send an `Idempotency-Key`. A replay with the same key and the same ids within 24 hours returns the stored result. After 24 hours the same ids still return the original success. A key reused with different ids is refused with `422 idempotency_mismatch`, permanently: a key stays bound to the ids it first succeeded with. Refusals are not stored, so a retry after a refusal runs again.

A merge sends an `identity.reconciled` webhook, including a merge that moved nothing. An analytics-only move sends none.

**Limits.** 300 calls a minute and 50,000 a day per project, counted separately from link-token presentations. Over a limit the response is `429` with `Retry-After`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key for this reconcile, 1 to 255 characters. A key stays bound to the ids it first succeeded with: reuse it only when retrying the same call.

from.description: The id to merge away, usually the guest id. Ids are matched without regard to letter case.

into.description: The id that keeps the purchases, usually the account id. If this id was merged away earlier, ZeroSettle follows it to the id that kept it.

reason.description: Optional note stored on the reconciliation record.

200.description: The ids were reconciled, or this is the replay of an earlier success.

400.description: `idempotency_key_required` (the `Idempotency-Key` header is missing or longer than 255 characters) or `invalid_request` (the body is not JSON with string `from` and `into` of at most 255 characters, or `reason` is longer than 500).

error.message: Send an Idempotency-Key header of 1 to 255 characters.

401.description: `secret_key_required`: no key, a publishable key, or a secret key that is not valid.

error.message: That secret key is not valid.

409.description: `reconcile_refused`. Nothing moved. The specific reason is on the customer page in the dashboard, not in this response.

error.message: The ids could not be reconciled. See the dashboard for details.

422.description: `idempotency_mismatch`. The `Idempotency-Key` is already bound to different ids.

error.message: This Idempotency-Key was already used with different ids.
Too many reconcile calls. Retry later.

post.description:
Mints a short-lived link token for an app to present with its publishable key (see Present Link Token). Use it when you want the app to finish the move instead of calling Reconcile Identities yourself.

Authenticated with your **secret key** (`zs_sk_*`). The token names one `from` and one `into`, expires after 10 minutes, and can be used once. Minting does not check the ids: the checks happen when the token is presented. You can also sign tokens yourself with no network call, see the Guest to Account guide for the exact format.

from.description: The id to merge away, usually the guest id. Ids are matched without regard to letter case.

into.description: The id that keeps the purchases, usually the account id.

token.description: The signed link token. Pass it to the SDK's `reconcile(linkToken:)`.

400.description: `invalid_request`. The body is not JSON with string `from` and `into` of at most 255 characters.

error.message: Send a JSON body with "from" and "into" ids of at most 255 characters.

401.description: `secret_key_required`: no key, a publishable key, or a secret key that is not valid.

error.message: That secret key is not valid.

post.description:
Called by the SDK (`reconcile(linkToken:)`) to finish a guest-to-account move with a link token your server signed. Authenticated with the publishable key.

The token is single use. It is spent when presented, even if the reconcile is refused. A `429` does not spend it. Limits: the project reconcile limits (300 a minute and 50,000 a day, counted apart from the secret-key endpoint), and 5 presentations an hour for the same `from` id. That per-id limit fails closed: if the rate-limit store is unavailable the call returns `429` with `Retry-After: 5`.

A merge sends an `identity.reconciled` webhook with `actor` of `link_token`.

link_token.description: The token from Create Link Token or your own signing.

400.description: `invalid_request`. `link_token` is missing or not a string.

error.message: Send a JSON body with a "link_token" string.

401.description: `invalid_link_token`: the token is malformed, has a bad signature, is expired, was already used, or is for the other environment. An invalid publishable key is also `401`, in the standard error shape.

error.message: That link token is not valid.

409.description: `reconcile_refused`. Nothing moved and the token is spent.

error.message: The ids could not be reconciled. See the dashboard for details.
Too many presentations for this id. Retry later.

post.description:
Moves a guest id's experiment and analytics rows to the signed-in id, from the app, with the publishable key. Use it to keep a pre-login funnel and experiment assignment when the person logs in.

**Without `link_token`** this endpoint never moves purchases and never touches a customer record. It moves experiment impressions, assignments, exposures, outcome rows and funnel events from `previous_user_id` (or `previous_install_id`) to `user_id`. It skips an id that a live account owns, and an id that was already merged away, and answers `status: "skipped"` with zero counts. Where `user_id` already holds a row for the same experiment, that row wins and the guest's row is left in place. Nothing is dropped.

**With `link_token`** it is a full reconcile, the same as Present Link Token: purchases move too, the same limits and refusals apply, and the response also carries `reconciliation_id`. Ids sent beside a token must both be present and match the token, or neither.

Without a token it is rate limited to 60 calls a minute per client IP and 6,000 a minute per app. Over a limit the response is `429` with `Retry-After`.

previous_user_id.description: The guest id to move rows from. Send this or `previous_install_id`.

previous_install_id.description: The raw SDK install id, as an alternative to `previous_user_id`.

user_id.description: The signed-in id to move rows to.

link_token.description: Optional. A link token from Create Link Token. With it, this is a full reconcile.

status.description: `skipped` when the guest id belongs to a live account or was merged away and no token was sent. Counts are then zero.

reconciliation_id.description: Present only when a `link_token` was sent.

400.description: `user_id` and one of `previous_user_id` or `previous_install_id` are required, or the body is not valid JSON.

401.description: `invalid_link_token`, when a `link_token` was sent and is not valid. An invalid publishable key is also `401`.

error.message: That link token is not valid.

409.description: `reconcile_refused`. Only with a `link_token`: nothing moved and the token is spent.

error.message: The ids could not be reconciled. See the dashboard for details.
Too many identity links. Retry later.

SecretKeyAuth.name: X-ZeroSettle-Key
SecretKeyAuth.description: Your secret API key (`zs_sk_test_*` or `zs_sk_live_*`). Server-side only: never ship a secret key in an app. Only the endpoints that say so accept it.

web_price.description: The web checkout price, or null if not available for web purchase.

mode.description: How the trial is collected. `free`: no charge during the trial period; the payment method is saved and billed at trial end. `paid`: a real upfront charge of `upfront_amount_cents` is collected immediately and kept; the full subscription price is billed at trial end. `auth_hold`: a temporary authorization hold of `hold_amount_cents` is placed (shown as a pending charge); released when the subscription converts or is cancelled.

duration.description: Duration token for the trial period (for example `1_week`, `3_days`, `1_month`), the same value as `free_trial_duration`. This is a ZeroSettle token, not an ISO 8601 duration.

hold_amount_cents.description: For `auth_hold` mode: the authorization hold amount placed at checkout, in cents. Zero for `free` and `paid` modes.

validates_card.description: `true` for `paid` and `auth_hold` modes (a real or pending charge verifies the card); `false` for `free` mode.

synced_to_asc.description: Whether the product has been synced to App Store Connect.

play_base_plan_id.description: The Google Play base plan ID for subscriptions, or null.

base_price_cents.description: The un-regionalized list price in cents.

sheet_type.description: Checkout presentation for this jurisdiction. `webview` is the default and the supported choice. `native_pay` is not supported for new integrations.

status.description: Transaction status as sent to SDKs. A successful payment is `completed`. A disputed transaction is reported as `refunded`. Abandoned checkout sessions are not returned.

storekit_status.description: StoreKit finish status: `1` = active, `2` = anything-not-active. Null for web checkout transactions.
